mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to reduced risk-free discounting of future cash flows.
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative during high-rate periods, or the FEDFUNDS spike is not statistically associated with negative excess returns (Granger causality p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls by more than 0.2 percentage points in a month, labor market strength is interpreted as supporting corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In 10 consecutive such UNRATE declines, the 60-day forward return is not statistically superior to a control group (mean difference < 0.5%, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in consumer inflation-adjusted housing starts (HOUST) of at least 5% signals weakening demand, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly < previous * 0.95 for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Early stage of housing market softening
failure_condition: During 8 such HOUST declines, the 5-day forward return is not statistically negative (mean > -0.2%, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly expansion in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average by at least 3% is interpreted as a supply-side acceleration, which produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
regime_hint: Economic expansion with strong output momentum
failure_condition: Across 10 such INDPRO expansions, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (mean ≤ 0.1%, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of CPIAUCSL to GDPC1 (real GDP deflator to personal income) rises by more than 0.5% in a month, it indicates a shift toward services-dominated demand, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: In 8 such CPIAUCSL/GDPC1 ratios, the 60-day forward return is not statistically negative (mean ≥ 0.2%, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden jump in monthly payroll employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 100,000 jobs in a single month predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days, reflecting market anticipation of stronger earnings.
failure_condition: During 6 such payroll spikes, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (mean ≤ 0.1%, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in retail sales (not directly observable in the catalog, but proxy via RSAFS as a demand indicator) of at least 10% signal a demand shock, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly < previous * 0.9 for two consecutive months and RSAFS < 1000K
failure_condition: During 4 such RSAFS contractions, the 5-day forward return is not statistically negative (mean ≥ -0.1%, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of falling consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) below 200 over three consecutive months indicates persistent cost pressures, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In 12 such deflationary triplets, the 20-day forward return is not statistically negative (mean ≥ -0.05%, p > 0.05).
